classes.name: Core\Arr
classes.summary:
`array<T>` is an insertion-ordered hash with copy-on-write value semantics
([ADR 0007 § 5](../decisions/0007.md)). Every member is pure (R3); an implementation
mutates in place whenever the argument's refcount is 1, so purity costs nothing. `T` is a type variable —
the stdlib is parametric where user code is not.

Every key is a `string`, so every key-valued **return** below is typed `string`; a key **parameter** is
`int|string`, matching the subscript normalisation of that same section. How arrays combine, and why no
member is named `merge`, is `rule:types/array-combination`.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to partition.

params.descHtml: Called as ($value, $key) per entry, and may declare fewer parameters; it answers the bucket's name, an int or a string.

doc.returnHtml: One inner array per distinct answer, in first-occurrence order, each keeping its entries under their own keys; 1 and "1" name one bucket.

doc.shortHtml: The entries added up, as array_sum does, promoting entry by entry: int with int stays int, a float anywhere makes the total float, a decimal anywhere makes it decimal.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The numbers to multiply.

doc.returnHtml: The product, of the widest type met; 1 as an int for the empty array.

errors.descHtml: The running int or decimal product leaves its type's range — there is no silent promotion to float — or a float and a decimal meet in one array, which have no common type.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The numbers to average.

doc.shortHtml: The largest entry under the natural order, as max with an array argument does — the order sort uses without a comparator, never PHP's loose comparison.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to search.

doc.returnHtml: The largest value, the first of equals; null for the empty array. Two strings compare bytewise, so max(["1e2", "50"]) is "50".

errors.descHtml: Two entries have no natural order between them — an int against a string, or any object.

members.name: sort
members.signature: sort(array<T> $a, {by?: callable, order?: Order, comparator?: callable, preserveKeys?: bool}): array<T>

doc.shortHtml: The entries in order, stably — sort, rsort, asort, arsort, usort, uasort, natsort, natcasesort and array_multisort as one member and four options.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to sort.

params.name: by
params.descHtml: Called once per entry as ($value, $key), and may declare fewer parameters; what it answers is compared in the entry's place.

params.name: order
params.descHtml: Order::Asc (the default) or Order::Desc, which reverses the comparison rather than the result, so equal entries keep their relative order either way.

params.name: comparator
params.descHtml: Called as ($a, $b) on two values — or on two by answers — and answering a negative, zero or positive number, as usort's callback does; it replaces the natural order.

params.name: preserveKeys
params.descHtml: Keep each entry's own key, as asort does; the default renumbers from "0", as sort does.

doc.returnHtml: The sorted entries. The natural order is between two numbers, two strings bytewise, two bools or two nulls — "10" sorts before "9" — and nothing else.

errors.descHtml: Two entries have no natural order between them — an int against a string, or any object — and no comparator was given; or the comparator answered NaN.

doc.shortHtml: The entries in key order, stably, every key kept — ksort, krsort and uksort as one member.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to sort.

params.name: order
params.descHtml: Order::Asc (the default) or Order::Desc, which reverses the comparison rather than the result, so equal keys keep their insertion order either way.

params.name: comparator
params.descHtml: Called as ($a, $b) on two keys, both strings, and answering a negative, zero or positive number, as uksort's callback does; it replaces the natural order.

doc.returnHtml: The same entries under the same keys, ordered by key; the natural order is bytewise, so "10" precedes "9".

errors.descHtml: The comparator answered NaN.

classes.summaryHtml:
array<T> is an insertion-ordered hash with copy-on-write value semantics (ADR 0007 § 5). Every member is pure (R3); an implementation mutates in place whenever the argument's refcount is 1, so purity costs nothing. T is a type variable — the stdlib is parametric where user code is not.

Every key is a string, so every key-valued return below is typed string; a key parameter is int|string, matching the subscript normalisation of that same section. How arrays combine, and why no member is named merge, is rule:types/array-combination.

params.descHtml: Where the window starts; negative counts from the end, and one before the start clamps to it.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many bytes to take; negative stops that many short of the end, and null, the default, runs to the end.

doc.returnHtml: The window as a new buffer; the empty buffer for an offset past the end or a window that closes before it opens.

members.name: indexOf
members.notes: no `caseInsensitive` option — case is a text concept
members.notesHtml: no caseInsensitive option — case is a text concept

doc.shortHtml: Finds where $needle first occurs in $haystack, as strpos does on binary data, as a byte offset slice takes directly. There is no case-insensitive option, because a byte string has no case.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The buffer searched.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The bytes looked for; an empty needle is found where the search starts.

params.name: from
params.descHtml: The byte offset the search starts at; negative counts from the end, and the default is 0.

doc.returnHtml: The byte offset of the first occurrence at or after from, or null when there is none — never false.

members.name: compare
members.notes: lexicographic octet order
members.notesHtml: lexicographic octet order

doc.shortHtml: Orders $a against $b lexicographically over unsigned octets, as strcmp does on binary data; a shorter buffer that is a prefix of a longer one sorts first. For equality alone, == is the operator.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first buffer.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The second buffer.

doc.returnHtml: -1, 0 or 1 — exactly those three, as PHP 8's strcmp answers.

doc.shortHtml: Tells whether $needle occurs anywhere in $haystack, as str_contains does on binary data.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The buffer searched.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The bytes looked for.

doc.returnHtml: true when it occurs; an empty needle is contained in every buffer, the empty one included.

doc.shortHtml: Tells whether $b begins with $prefix, as str_starts_with does on binary data — the member a magic-byte sniff writes.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The buffer.

params.name: prefix
params.descHtml: The bytes it must begin with.

doc.returnHtml: true when it does; an empty prefix begins every buffer.

doc.shortHtml: Tells whether $b ends with $suffix, as str_ends_with does on binary data.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The buffer.

params.name: suffix
params.descHtml: The bytes it must end with.

doc.returnHtml: true when it does; an empty suffix ends every buffer.

doc.shortHtml: Concatenates every buffer in $parts with $separator between neighbours, as implode does on binary data — Core\Str::join's row over buffers, and this class's only concatenation. No element is converted.

params.name: parts
params.descHtml: The buffers to join, in order.

params.name: separator
params.descHtml: The bytes written between neighbours; the empty buffer by default.

doc.returnHtml: The new buffer; the empty buffer for no parts.

errors.descHtml: The result is larger than any buffer this process could hold.

members.name: fill
members.notes: a `$byte` above 255 throws
members.notesHtml: a $byte above 255 throws

doc.shortHtml: Builds a buffer of $length copies of the octet $byte, as the str_repeat(chr($b), $n) idiom does; a zero-filled header is fill(16, 0).

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many octets to write.

params.name: byte
params.descHtml: The octet repeated, 0 to 255.

doc.returnHtml: The new buffer; the empty buffer for a length of 0.

errors.descHtml: $byte is above 255, or $length is larger than any buffer this process could hold.

doc.shortHtml: Builds a buffer of $b repeated $times times, as str_repeat does on binary data.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The buffer repeated.

params.name: times
params.descHtml: How many copies to write.

doc.returnHtml: The new buffer; the empty buffer for a count of 0 or an empty subject.

errors.descHtml: $times, or the result, is larger than any buffer this process could hold.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $values as the octets $format describes, as pack does, over a closed code table: a/A/Z a buffer NUL-padded, space-padded, or NUL-padded and NUL-terminated; c/C one octet; n/v, N/V and J/P 16, 32 and 64 bits most or least significant octet first; G/g binary32 and E/e binary64 the same way; x one NUL octet. A bare code takes the whole argument, never one octet, and an integer field takes the union of its width's signed and unsigned ranges in two's complement.

params.name: format
params.descHtml: The format string — an intrinsic and a sink, so a literal — where each code may be followed by a count or *: how many arguments a numeric field takes, and how many octets wide a buffer field is.

params.name: values
params.descHtml: The values written, one per numeric field and one buffer per buffer field; an integer field takes an int or a uint, a float field a float, and nothing is converted.

doc.returnHtml: The packed buffer.

errors.descHtml: $format holds a code outside the table — the machine-width codes s, S, i, I, l, L, q, Q, f and d, the hex codes h and H, and the cursor codes X and @ are refused naming the replacement — or x*, or a count larger than any buffer; a field's value is missing, of the wrong type, outside its width's range, a float outside binary32's range, or a buffer wider than its field; or the format writes fewer values than the call passed.

doc.shortHtml: Reads $b back through $format, as unpack does, over pack's code table in reverse — so unpack(pack($f, ...$v), $f) is $v, field for field. Octets the format does not describe throw rather than being ignored.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The buffer read.

params.name: format
params.descHtml: The same format string pack takes, an intrinsic and a sink; there is no second grammar for field names.

doc.returnHtml: The fields as a positional list, never PHP's name-keyed map: an int for c, a uint for every other integer code, a float for G/g/E/e, and a bytes for a buffer code with A's and Z's padding taken back off.

errors.descHtml: $format holds a code outside the table or a count larger than any buffer, a field reads past the end of $b, or octets are left over after the last field.

members.name: parse
members.signature: parse(string $text, {separator?, quote?, escape?, header?: bool}): array<array<string>>

doc.shortHtml: Parses the whole CSV document $text into its records, as str_getcsv and the parsing half of fgetcsv do, by RFC 4180's grammar: a field is quoted or it is not, a doubled quote inside a quoted field is one quote, a record ends at LF or CRLF, and a blank line is not a record.

params.name: text
params.descHtml: The CSV document, whole.

params.name: separator
params.descHtml: The single ASCII byte between fields; , by default.

params.name: quote
params.descHtml: The single ASCII byte that quotes a field; " by default.

params.name: escape
params.descHtml: The single ASCII byte that escapes a quote inside a quoted field, or the empty string for none, which is the default — a doubled quote is the RFC's own escape.

params.name: header
params.descHtml: Consume the first record as column names and key every returned row by them; the default keys each field by its column index.

doc.returnHtml: One array per record, every field a string, keyed by column index or — with header — by the header's names, a field past the header's last name keeping its index; the header row itself is not returned. The document itself never fails to parse, and an empty document is the empty array.

errors.descHtml: A dialect option is empty, longer than one ASCII character, or CR or LF; or two of separator, quote and escape name the same byte.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $rows as a CSV document, as fputcsv's formatting half does over a whole document: a field is quoted exactly when it holds the separator, the quote, CR or LF, a quote inside one is doubled, and every record ends with LF, so parse(format($rows)) answers $rows.

params.name: rows
params.descHtml: The records to write, each an array of string fields taken in order; a row's keys are ignored.

params.name: separator
params.descHtml: The single ASCII byte written between fields; , by default.

params.name: quote
params.descHtml: The single ASCII byte that quotes a field; " by default.

params.name: header
params.descHtml: Column names written as the first record; null, the default, writes no header row.

doc.returnHtml: The document; the empty string for no rows and no header.

errors.descHtml: A dialect option is empty, longer than one ASCII character, or CR or LF; or separator and quote name the same byte.

members.name: rows
members.signature: rows(Core\IO\File $file, {separator?, quote?, escape?, header?: bool}): Core\Csv\Rows

doc.shortHtml: Walks an open file one record at a time, as while ($r = fgetcsv($h)) does, by the same RFC 4180 grammar and the same dialect parse reads. The walk holds one record and never the document, so a file larger than memory reads fine; it reads forward from wherever the handle is and is taken once.

params.name: file
params.descHtml: The open handle to read from, positioned where the walk should start.

params.name: separator
params.descHtml: The single ASCII byte between fields; , by default.

params.name: quote
params.descHtml: The single ASCII byte that quotes a field; " by default.

params.name: escape
params.descHtml: The single ASCII byte that escapes a quote inside a quoted field, or the empty string for none, which is the default — a doubled quote is the RFC's own escape.

params.name: header
params.descHtml: Consume the first record as column names and key every walked record by them; the default keys each field by its column index.

doc.returnHtml: A walk over the records, each an array of string fields keyed as parse keys one. Nothing is read until the walk is taken.

errors.descHtml: A dialect option is empty, longer than one ASCII character, or CR or LF; two of separator, quote and escape name the same byte; or the handle was closed before or during the walk.
The operating system refused a read part way through the walk.

classes.name: Core\Db
classes.summary:
Semantics are `rule:core-classes/db-one-api` — connection naming and memoization, the capability split,
why there is no `prepare`, the transaction shape, the coercion rule and the full SQL type map. This section
owns the signatures only. Every member needs `db.connect` or `db.open`, and a connection's credentials live
in a root-owned `[db.<name>]` block (`rule:config/the-file-is-nvs-toml-and-it-is-toml`).
classes.surface: the full surface is § 18 below — the one subsystem in Part II too large for a row. Replaces `PDO` **and** the procedural `mysqli`/`pgsql`/`sqlite3` APIs

doc.shortHtml: Opens the connection an operator named in a [db.<name>] block of nvs.toml, and answers the same one again for the rest of the request — new PDO, pg_connect and mysqli_connect, with the credential out of the program and in root-owned configuration. Needs the db.connect capability for that name.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The block to open, matched exactly: "main" is [db.main]. Two blocks that configure the same server are two connections, because an operator who wrote two meant two.

params.name: shared
params.descHtml: Whether this call may answer with the connection an earlier one already opened. false opens a dedicated connection instead — what a write that must survive a rollback, a session-scoped lock or a second statement alongside a stream needs.

params.name: timeout
params.descHtml: How long the handshake may take, including name resolution and TLS. Left out, the connection is bounded by the server and the network alone.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Db\Connection. The same call twice in one request answers the same object unless shared is false, and the connection is closed when the request ends.

errors.descHtml: db.connect does not grant $name, no [db.<name>] block of that name exists, or the block cannot be read as a connection — a missing driver, a field belonging to another driver, or a time_zone that is not an offset.

The host does not resolve, the connection, the TLS handshake or the login itself failed, or this core already holds [db.<name>.pool] max connections under that name and none came free within acquire. A refusal the server worded carries its own message.

doc.shortHtml: Opens a connection to a server the program itself names, for the case a [db.<name>] block cannot cover — a tenant whose database is a row in another one, or an administration tool a human types a host into. Needs the db.open capability for that host, and unlike connect the address is checked against the denied ranges in full.

params.name: settings
params.descHtml: Everything the connection is made of. It is one of two shapes and the driver decides which: four of the five backends take a host, and SQLite takes a file path instead.

shape.descHtml: Which backend this is, and so which of the two shapes the rest of the literal has to be.
The server to open, and the name its certificate is checked against. It is a sink with no launderer: no check on a string can establish that a host is safe to send a credential to.
The port to open. Left out, the driver's own — 5432 for PostgreSQL, 3306 for MySQL and MariaDB.
The database or schema to attach to. tainted is accepted: it is a length-prefixed protocol field and never parsed text.
The role to log in as, accepted tainted for the same reason.
The role's password. It is secret, so it cannot reach a log line, a message or a trace.
How much of the certificate is checked. Only VerifyFull runs, and it is what an absent key means; the weaker three are refused.
The zone a column with no zone of its own is read in, and the one the server is told to use. UTC where it is absent.
How long the handshake may take, resolution and TLS included.
How many prepared statements this connection may keep on the server. 0 turns the cache off.
SQLite's file, in place of a host. It is a path sink, and reaching it needs fs.read and fs.write as well.

params.name: shared
params.descHtml: Whether this call may answer with the connection an earlier one opened from the same settings. false opens a dedicated connection instead.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Db\Connection, closed when the request ends. Two calls with settings that agree in every field answer the same object unless shared is false.

errors.descHtml: db.open does not grant the host, the address it resolves to is a private range that net.internal does not except, the settings do not describe a connection this build can open, or tls asks for a mode weaker than VerifyFull.
The host does not resolve, the connection, the TLS handshake or the login itself failed, or this core already holds its max of connections to those settings and none came free while waiting.

doc.shortHtml: Marks $values as a run of bound values rather than one, so the placeholder it is bound to expands into a parenthesised list of that many — the IN (?, ?, ?) every PHP program builds with implode and array_fill. Nothing else in a statement expands, which is what keeps the SQL text independent of what a value turned out to be.

params.name: values
params.descHtml: The values to bind, one placeholder each, in the array's own order. Keys are not read: a marker binds positions inside one placeholder, not names.

doc.returnHtml: A Core\Db\InList to bind to a single placeholder. It has no members and is accepted nowhere else; two lists of different lengths bound to the same SQL are two entries in the statement cache, because expansion changes the statement's arity.

errors.descHtml: $values is empty, which means "match nothing" inside IN and "match everything" inside NOT IN — the caller branches instead.

doc.shortHtml: Checks that $name is a bare SQL identifier — a letter or _, then letters, digits or _ — and answers it unchanged and no longer tainted, so it can be written into the text of a statement. Replaces escaping a table or column name by hand, which is what mysqli_real_escape_string was doing there.

params.name: name
params.descHtml: The identifier to check. It is answered exactly as given: nothing is escaped, truncated or lower-cased, because a name this accepts needs none of it.

doc.returnHtml: The same text, without the tainted qualifier. It carries no delimiter — Core\Db has no connection and so no dialect, and the five backends disagree on what a delimiter is.

errors.descHtml: $name is empty, starts with a digit, or holds any character outside letters, digits and _ — including a name that would need delimiting to be legal.

classes.summaryHtml: Semantics are rule:core-classes/db-one-api — connection naming and memoization, the capability split, why there is no prepare, the transaction shape, the coercion rule and the full SQL type map. This section owns the signatures only. Every member needs db.connect or db.open, and a connection's credentials live in a root-owned [db.<name>] block (rule:config/the-file-is-nvs-toml-and-it-is-toml).

classes.name: Core\Encoding
classes.summary:
`Core\Encoding` sits exactly at the `bytes`↔`string` boundary, which is the one place a conversion can
honestly fail (`rule:types/bytes`).

doc.shortHtml: Reads the octets $b as $charset into a string, as iconv, mb_convert_encoding and utf8_decode do — exactly: a sequence the charset cannot read throws rather than becoming U+FFFD or being dropped.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The octets to decode.

params.name: charset
params.descHtml: The encoding they are in.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded text; the empty string for the empty buffer.

errors.descHtml: A byte sequence of $b is not valid $charset; the message names its offset.

doc.shortHtml: Writes $s as $charset's octets, as iconv, mb_convert_encoding and utf8_encode do — exactly, with no //IGNORE or //TRANSLIT mode: a character the charset cannot spell throws rather than becoming ? or &#NNNN;.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to encode.

params.name: charset
params.descHtml: The encoding to write.

doc.returnHtml: The encoded octets.

errors.descHtml: $charset has no spelling for a character of $s; the message names the character and its offset.

doc.shortHtml: Tells whether every byte sequence in $b is one $charset reads, as mb_check_encoding does — decodeText's question without the throw.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The octets to check.

params.name: charset
params.descHtml: The encoding they are checked against.

doc.returnHtml: true when decodeText would succeed; always true under Charset::Latin1, which gives all 256 octets a meaning.

doc.shortHtml: Spells $b in RFC 4648 § 4's base64 alphabet, padded — byte for byte what base64_encode answers.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The octets to encode.

doc.returnHtml: The base64 text; the empty string for the empty buffer.

doc.shortHtml: Reads base64 text $s back to octets, as base64_decode does in strict mode and stricter: § 4's alphabet only, padding required and canonical, and no unread bits in the last symbol. URL-safe text is fromBase64Url's to read.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The base64 text.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded octets; the empty buffer for the empty string.

errors.descHtml: $s is not strict base64 — a symbol outside the alphabet, - and _ included, missing or wrong padding, a truncated final group, or non-canonical trailing bits.

doc.shortHtml: Spells $b in RFC 4648 § 5's URL-safe base64 alphabet, unpadded — the rtrim(strtr(base64_encode($b), "+/", "-_"), "=") idiom, as a JWT or a query string expects it.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The octets to encode.

doc.returnHtml: The URL-safe base64 text; the empty string for the empty buffer.

doc.shortHtml: Reads URL-safe base64 text $s back to octets — toBase64Url's other half, as strict as fromBase64 and refusing padding rather than tolerating it.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The URL-safe base64 text, unpadded.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded octets; the empty buffer for the empty string.

errors.descHtml: $s is not unpadded URL-safe base64 — a symbol outside the alphabet, +, / and = included, a truncated final group, or non-canonical trailing bits.

doc.shortHtml: Spells $b as lowercase hexadecimal, two digits per octet, as bin2hex and the unpack("H*", …) idiom do.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The octets to encode.

doc.returnHtml: The hex text, twice $b's length; the empty string for the empty buffer.

doc.shortHtml: Reads hexadecimal text $s back to octets, as hex2bin does but throwing where it warned and answered false: either case, two digits per octet, and nothing between the pairs.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The hexadecimal text.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded octets, half as many as $s has digits; the empty buffer for the empty string.

errors.descHtml: $s has an odd number of digits, or a character that is not 0-9, a-f or A-F — a space, a colon or a 0x prefix included.

doc.shortHtml: Spells $b in RFC 4648 § 6's base32 alphabet, upper case and unpadded — the form an otpauth: secret is written in; PHP has no counterpart.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The octets to encode.

doc.returnHtml: The base32 text; the empty string for the empty buffer.

doc.shortHtml: Reads base32 text $s back to octets — toBase32's other half, taking either case and padding that is canonical or absent, since neither changes which octets come out.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The base32 text.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded octets; the empty buffer for the empty string.

errors.descHtml: $s holds a symbol outside the alphabet — a space between groups included — a truncated final group, non-canonical trailing bits, or padding that is present but wrong.

classes.summaryHtml: Core\Encoding sits exactly at the bytes↔string boundary, which is the one place a conversion can honestly fail (rule:types/bytes).

doc.shortHtml: Computes the digest of $data under $digest, replacing hash, md5, sha1, crc32 and openssl_digest at once — raw octets, never hex or an int.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The octets to hash; a string is read as its UTF-8 bytes.

params.name: digest
params.descHtml: The algorithm, any Core\Digest case — the broken ones included, for interop.

doc.returnHtml: The digest as bytes, as many octets as the case's width; every case accepts every input, the empty one included.

doc.shortHtml: Computes RFC 2104's HMAC of $data under $key and $digest, as hash_hmac does without its raw_output flag — and only under a StrongDigest, so Digest::Md5 or Digest::Sha1 here is a compile error.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The octets to authenticate; a string is read as its UTF-8 bytes.

params.name: key
params.descHtml: The secret key, of any length — a long one is hashed down and a short one zero-padded, as RFC 2104 § 2 says.

params.name: digest
params.descHtml: The algorithm, one of the ten SHA-2 and SHA-3 Core\Digest cases.

doc.returnHtml: The MAC as bytes, as many octets as the case's width.

doc.shortHtml: Compares two digests in constant time, as hash_equals does: the running time does not depend on where two equal-length operands first differ.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: One digest.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The other digest.

doc.returnHtml: true when the two hold the same octets; false at once for two lengths that differ, since a digest's length is the algorithm's and never a secret.

doc.shortHtml: Opens an incremental digest under $digest, as hash_init does — a Core\Hash\Stream fed by update and closed by finish.

params.name: digest
params.descHtml: The algorithm, any Core\Digest case.

doc.returnHtml: A fresh, open stream that has been fed nothing yet.

doc.shortHtml: Feeds $data to the stream, as hash_update does; the chunks are digested in order at finish.

params.name: data
params.descHtml: The next octets; a string is read as its UTF-8 bytes.

doc.returnHtml: Nothing; the stream holds a reference to $data until finish.

errors.descHtml: The stream has already been finished — a digest is final, so open a new stream.

doc.shortHtml: Closes the stream and answers the digest of everything update fed it, as hash_final does — the same octets Core\Hash::of answers over the concatenation.
doc.returnHtml: The digest as bytes; the stream is finished afterwards and its chunks released.

errors.descHtml: The stream has already been finished — a second finish is refused rather than continuing from the first.

doc.shortHtml: Serializes $value as JSON text — scalars, arrays, shape literals and instances of classes carrying #[Json\Derive] — on one line unless pretty is set.

params.name: value
params.descHtml: The value to encode: null, bool, int, uint, float, decimal, string, an array, a {name: value} shape, or an instance of a class carrying #[Json\Derive].

params.name: pretty
params.descHtml: Indent the output across lines, as JSON_PRETTY_PRINT does; the default is one line.

params.name: escapeUnicode
params.descHtml: Write every non-ASCII character as a \uXXXX escape, as json_encode does by default; the default here keeps UTF-8 as it is.

doc.returnHtml: The JSON text.

errors.descHtml: $value holds something JSON cannot spell: a NaN or infinite float, a value of a type with no JSON encoding, an instance of a class without #[Json\Derive], or nesting past 1024 levels.

doc.shortHtml: Parses the JSON text $json into a value, as json_decode does with $associative set: an object becomes a string-keyed array, an array a list, and a scalar itself. A malformed document throws rather than answering null, so there is no json_last_error.

params.name: json
params.descHtml: The JSON text to parse.

params.name: maxDepth
params.descHtml: The deepest nesting accepted, counted as PHP's $depth is — a scalar document is depth 1, [1] is depth 2; 512 by default and at most 1024.

doc.returnHtml: The decoded value: null, bool, int, float, string, or an array; a JSON object is always a string-keyed array, never an object.

errors.descHtml: $json is not a valid JSON document, nests deeper than maxDepth, or holds an integer literal too large for int; the one issue it carries has an empty path.
maxDepth is 0 or above 1024.

doc.shortHtml: Parses the JSON object $json into an instance of T, a class carrying #[Json\Derive], reading every declared field and running the constructor only when all of them matched; write array<T> to read a JSON array as one instance per element instead. It replaces hand-written hydration.

params.name: json
params.descHtml: The JSON text to parse, whose top level must be an object — or an array, where T is written array<C>.

params.name: maxDepth
params.descHtml: The deepest nesting accepted, counted as PHP's $depth is — a scalar document is depth 1, [1] is depth 2; 512 by default and at most 1024.

doc.returnHtml: A new T built from the document's fields, or — for an array<C> — one new C per element, in the document's own order.

errors.descHtml: $json is not a valid JSON document, nests deeper than maxDepth, holds an integer literal too large for int, is not an object at the top level (an array, for an array<C>), or has fields that are missing or of the wrong type — every failed field is one issue on the error, at its own path, and the message counts them. A list stops at its first bad element, and each of its paths carries that element's position.
T has no JSON codec because it does not carry #[Json\Derive], or maxDepth is 0 or above 1024.
The call stack is full before the last object is created. This can happen when a class contains itself and the document nests very deeply.

doc.shortHtml: Tells whether $json is a document decode would accept at the default depth of 512, as json_validate does, by parsing it.

params.name: json
params.descHtml: The JSON text to check.

doc.returnHtml: true when $json parses; false for malformed text, nesting past 512, or an integer literal too large for int.

classes.name: Core\Math
classes.summary:
`**` is exponentiation and `%` is integer modulo, so neither has a member (R17). Division by zero throws
`ArithmeticError` (R4) — in `intDiv`, in `mod`, and in the `/` operator whatever the operand types, which
is exactly why `fdiv` *is* a member here: it is the one spelling left for IEEE's `INF`, and PHP has it for
the same reason. Overflow throws rather than becoming a `float`
(`rule:types/arithmetic`).

enums.name: RoundMode
enums.raw: RoundMode { HalfUp, HalfDown, HalfEven, HalfOdd, Up, Down }

doc.shortHtml: How Core\Math::round settles a value between two neighbours — PHP's four PHP_ROUND_HALF_* constants plus the two whole-direction rules ceil and floor only cover at a precision of zero.

cases.name: HalfUp
cases.descHtml: A tie goes away from zero — PHP_ROUND_HALF_UP, and round's default there and here.

cases.name: HalfDown
cases.descHtml: A tie goes toward zero — PHP_ROUND_HALF_DOWN.

cases.name: HalfEven
cases.descHtml: A tie goes to the even neighbour — banker's rounding, PHP_ROUND_HALF_EVEN, the rule that does not accumulate a bias over many values.

cases.name: HalfOdd
cases.descHtml: A tie goes to the odd neighbour — PHP_ROUND_HALF_ODD.

cases.name: Up
cases.descHtml: Every value goes away from zero, tie or not — ceil for a positive number and floor for a negative one, at any precision.

cases.name: Down
cases.descHtml: Every value goes toward zero, tie or not — truncation, at any precision.

constants.name: PI
constants.descHtml: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, 3.14159… as the nearest float — PHP's M_PI.

constants.name: TAU
constants.descHtml: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its radius, 2 PI or 6.28318… as the nearest float — a full turn in radians, which PHP spells 2 M_PI.

constants.name: E
constants.descHtml: Euler's number, the base of the natural logarithm, 2.71828… as the nearest float — PHP's M_E, and log's default base.

constants.name: EPSILON
constants.descHtml: The smallest float that added to 1.0 gives a value other than 1.0, 2.220446049250313e-16 — PHP's PHP_FLOAT_EPSILON, and the tolerance to compare two floats with in place of ==.

constants.name: INT_MIN
constants.descHtml: The smallest int, -9223372036854775808 — PHP's PHP_INT_MIN, and the one value abs has no int answer for.

constants.name: UINT_MAX
constants.descHtml: The largest uint, 18446744073709551615 — a type PHP does not have, so there is no constant to replace.

constants.name: FLOAT_MAX
constants.descHtml: The largest finite float, 1.7976931348623157e308 — PHP's PHP_FLOAT_MAX; the negative extreme is -FLOAT_MAX.

constants.name: FLOAT_MIN
constants.descHtml: The smallest positive normal float, 2.2250738585072014e-308 — PHP's PHP_FLOAT_MIN, and not the negative extreme, which is -FLOAT_MAX.

constants.name: NAN
constants.descHtml: The float that is not a number — PHP's NAN — equal to nothing, itself included, so isNan is the only test for it.

constants.name: INFINITY
constants.descHtml: Positive infinity as a float, past every finite value — PHP's INF; the negative one is -INFINITY, and isFinite is false for both.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $n without its sign, as the same kind of number. -3 gives 3 and -2.5 gives 2.5.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number whose sign is removed: an int, a float or a decimal.

doc.returnHtml: $n without its sign, with the same type as $n. An int gives an int, a uint is returned unchanged, a float gives a float and a decimal gives a decimal with the same decimal places. -0.0 becomes 0.0.

errors.descHtml: When $n is INT_MIN, whose positive value is one past INT_MAX.

doc.shortHtml: Returns -1 when $n is below zero, 1 when it is above zero and 0 when it is zero. This replaces PHP's $n <=> 0.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to check: an int, a float or a decimal.

doc.returnHtml: -1, 0 or 1, as an int. -0.0 is zero, so the result for it is 0.

errors.descHtml: When $n is NaN (a value that means "not a number"). NaN is not below, above or equal to zero.
When $n is a uint bigger than Core\Math::INT_MAX.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the smaller of two values. This replaces PHP's min with two values. For the smallest value in an array, use Core\Arr::min.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: One value: a number, a string, a bool or null.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The other value, of the same type as $a.

doc.returnHtml: The smaller value. When the two are equal, the result is $a. NaN is smaller than every other float.

errors.descHtml: When the two values cannot be compared: an object, an array, or two values of different kinds.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the larger of two values. This replaces PHP's max with two values. For the largest value in an array, use Core\Arr::max.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: One value: a number, a string, a bool or null.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The other value, of the same type as $a.

doc.returnHtml: The larger value. When the two are equal, the result is $a. NaN is smaller than every other float.

errors.descHtml: When the two values cannot be compared: an object, an array, or two values of different kinds.

doc.shortHtml: Keeps $n between $low and $high. It replaces PHP's min(max($n, $low), $high).

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The value to keep in the range. It can be a number, a string, a bool or null.

params.name: low
params.descHtml: The smallest value the result can be.

params.name: high
params.descHtml: The largest value the result can be. It must not be below $low.

doc.returnHtml: $low when $n is below it, $high when $n is above it, and $n itself otherwise. Both ends are inside the range.

errors.descHtml: When $low is above $high. Also when two of the values cannot be compared: an object without compareTo, an array, or a number and a string.

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $n up to the next whole number. For a negative $n, up means toward zero.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to round up.

doc.returnHtml: A whole number, as a float. A $n between -1.0 and 0.0 gives -0.0. NaN and the infinities stay the same.

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $n down to the next whole number. For a negative $n, down means away from zero.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to round down.

doc.returnHtml: A whole number, as a float. A $n between -1.0 and 0.0 gives -1.0. NaN and the infinities stay the same.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the fractional part of $n. The result moves toward zero, so 2.7 gives 2.0 and -2.7 gives -2.0.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number whose fractional part is removed.

doc.returnHtml: A whole number, as a float. A $n between -1.0 and 0.0 gives -0.0. NaN and the infinities stay the same.

doc.shortHtml: Rounds $n to a number of decimal places. This replaces PHP's round. The mode option chooses the result for a value exactly halfway between two results.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to round.

params.name: precision
params.descHtml: How many decimal places to keep. The default is 0, which rounds to a whole number. -2 rounds to hundreds.

params.name: mode
params.descHtml: A Core\RoundMode case. The default is RoundMode::HalfUp, which rounds a half away from zero.

doc.returnHtml: The rounded float. NaN and the infinities are returned unchanged. $n is also returned unchanged when precision is above 22 or below -22, or when $n * 10 precision is 2 53 or more.

doc.shortHtml: Divides $a by $b and drops the remainder, so the result moves toward zero. This replaces PHP's intdiv.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The integer to divide.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The integer to divide by. It may not be zero.

doc.returnHtml: The whole part of $a / $b. intDiv(7, 2) is 3, and intDiv(-7, 2) is -3. The % operator gives the remainder.

errors.descHtml: When $b is zero. Also when $a is Core\Math::INT_MIN and $b is -1, because the result is one more than Core\Math::INT_MAX.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the remainder after dividing $a by $b, for float values. The result has the sign of $a. This replaces PHP's fmod. For whole numbers, use the % operator.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The number to divide.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The number to divide by. It may not be zero.

doc.returnHtml: The remainder. mod(7.5, 2.0) is 1.5, and mod(-7.5, 2.0) is -1.5. When $a is an infinity, the result is NaN. When $b is an infinity, the result is $a.

errors.descHtml: When $b is zero. PHP's fmod returns NaN here.

doc.shortHtml: Divides $a by $b. When $b is zero, it returns INFINITY, -INFINITY or NaN. The / operator throws an error there. This replaces PHP's fdiv.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The number to divide.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The number to divide by. It may be zero.

doc.returnHtml: $a / $b. When $b is zero, the result is INFINITY or -INFINITY. Its sign comes from the signs of both numbers together. When both numbers are zero, the result is NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the greatest common divisor of two integers. This is the largest integer that divides both with no remainder. This replaces PHP's gmp_gcd.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first integer. Its sign does not change the result.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The second integer. Its sign does not change the result.

doc.returnHtml: The greatest common divisor, which is never negative. When one integer is 0, the result is the other one without its sign. When both are 0, the result is 0.

errors.descHtml: When the result does not fit an int. This happens only when one integer is Core\Math::INT_MIN and the other is Core\Math::INT_MIN or 0.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the least common multiple of two integers. This is the smallest positive integer that both divide with no remainder. This replaces PHP's gmp_lcm.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first integer. Its sign does not change the result.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The second integer. Its sign does not change the result.

doc.returnHtml: The least common multiple, which is never negative. When one integer is 0, the result is 0.

errors.descHtml: When the result is bigger than Core\Math::INT_MAX. This happens quickly for two big integers that share no divisor.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the square root of $n. This replaces PHP's sqrt.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to take the square root of.

doc.returnHtml: A float that is zero or more. A negative $n gives NaN. -0.0 gives -0.0, and Core\Math::INFINITY gives Core\Math::INFINITY.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the cube root of $n. A negative $n works too. PHP code often writes pow($n, 1/3), which gives NaN for a negative number.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: Any number.

doc.returnHtml: The cube root, with the same sign as $n: Core\Math::cbrt(-8.0) is -2.0. An infinity gives the same infinity, and NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the length of the longest side of a right triangle. $a and $b are the other two sides. The result is sqrt($a $a + $b $b), but it stays correct when $a * $a is too big for a float. This replaces PHP's hypot.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The length of one side. Its sign does not change the result.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The length of the other side. Its sign does not change the result.

doc.returnHtml: The length. It is never negative. When $a or $b is INFINITY or -INFINITY, the result is INFINITY, even when the other one is NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns E raised to the power $n. E is about 2.718. This replaces PHP's exp.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The power to raise E to.

doc.returnHtml: E ** $n, which is never negative. Above about 709.78 the result is INFINITY. Far enough below zero, the result is 0.0. NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the logarithm of $n: the power you raise base to to get $n. The base is E unless you give one. This replaces PHP's log, log10 and log2.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to take the logarithm of.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The base. It must be greater than zero, and it is E when you leave it out. For a power of 10.0 or 2.0 in that base, the result is exact.

doc.returnHtml: The logarithm. When $n is 0.0 and base is greater than 1.0, the result is -INFINITY. When $n is negative, or base is 1.0, the result is NaN.

errors.descHtml: When base is zero or negative. PHP throws a ValueError here.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the sine of an angle. The angle is in radians.

params.name: radians
params.descHtml: The angle, in radians. Core\Math::toRadians converts degrees to radians.

doc.returnHtml: A number from -1.0 to 1.0. An infinity or NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the cosine of an angle. The angle is in radians.

params.name: radians
params.descHtml: The angle, in radians. Core\Math::toRadians converts degrees to radians.

doc.returnHtml: A number from -1.0 to 1.0. An infinity or NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the tangent of an angle. The angle is in radians. The tangent is the sine divided by the cosine.

params.name: radians
params.descHtml: The angle, in radians. Core\Math::toRadians converts degrees to radians.

doc.returnHtml: Any number. It is very large when the angle is close to 90 degrees. An infinity or NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the angle, in radians, whose sine is $n. This is the arc sine.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: A sine: a number from -1.0 to 1.0.

doc.returnHtml: An angle from -PI / 2 to PI / 2, in radians. A $n outside -1.0 to 1.0 gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the angle, in radians, whose cosine is $n. This is the arc cosine.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: A cosine: a number from -1.0 to 1.0.

doc.returnHtml: An angle from 0.0 to PI, in radians. A $n outside -1.0 to 1.0 gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the angle, in radians, whose tangent is $n. This is the arc tangent. For a point, use Core\Math::atan2, which takes both coordinates.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: A tangent: any number.

doc.returnHtml: An angle between -PI / 2 and PI / 2, in radians. An infinite $n gives exactly PI / 2 or -PI / 2.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the angle of the point ($x, $y), in radians, measured from the positive x-axis. $y comes first.

params.name: y
params.descHtml: The point's y coordinate.

params.name: x
params.descHtml: The point's x coordinate.

doc.returnHtml: An angle from -PI to PI, in radians. A point above the x-axis gives a positive angle, and a point below it gives a negative one. The point (0, 0) gives 0.0.

doc.shortHtml: Converts an angle from degrees to radians. It computes ($degrees / 180) * PI, the same way as PHP.

params.name: degrees
params.descHtml: The angle, in degrees.

doc.returnHtml: The same angle in radians. Core\Math::toRadians(180.0) is PI. An infinity gives an infinity, and NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Converts an angle from radians to degrees. It computes ($radians / PI) * 180, the same way as PHP.

params.name: radians
params.descHtml: The angle, in radians.

doc.returnHtml: The same angle in degrees. Core\Math::toDegrees(Core\Math::PI) is 180.0. A result too big for a float is an infinity, and NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns true when $n is NaN, a value that means "not a number". NaN is not equal to any value, itself included, so == cannot find it. This replaces PHP's is_nan.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The value to test.

doc.returnHtml: true when $n is NaN. false for every other float, INFINITY and -INFINITY included.

doc.shortHtml: Returns true when $n is an ordinary number. INFINITY, -INFINITY and NaN are not ordinary numbers. This replaces PHP's is_finite. PHP's is_infinite($n) is !isFinite($n) && !isNan($n).

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The value to test.

doc.returnHtml: true for every ordinary float, zero included. false for INFINITY, -INFINITY and NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Writes the number $n in base $base and returns the digits as a string. This replaces PHP's decbin, dechex, decoct and base_convert. Digits above 9 are the lower case letters a to z.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to write. It can be negative.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The base, from 2 to 36. Base 2 is binary and base 16 is hexadecimal.

doc.returnHtml: The digits, with no prefix and no leading zeros. A negative $n starts with -. 0 returns "0".

errors.descHtml: When $base is outside 2 to 36. PHP's base_convert returns 0 here.

doc.shortHtml: Reads a number written in base $base and returns it as an int. This replaces PHP's bindec, hexdec, octdec and base_convert. Every character must be a digit of the base. PHP skips a character that is not.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The digits. A leading - is allowed. A prefix such as 0x, spaces and separators are not allowed. Letters can be upper or lower case.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The base, from 2 to 36. Digits above 9 are the letters a to z.

doc.returnHtml: The number as an int. Core\Math::toBase writes it back.

errors.descHtml: When $base is outside 2 to 36, when $s has no digits, or when a character of $s is not a digit of the base.
When the number is too large for an int.

members.name: format
members.signature: format(int|float|decimal $n, {decimals?: uint, decimalSeparator?: string, groupSeparator?: string}): string

doc.shortHtml: Writes a number as text for a person to read, with a fixed number of decimals. This replaces PHP's number_format. The digits are not grouped unless you give a groupSeparator.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: The number to write: an int, a float or a decimal.

params.name: decimals
params.descHtml: How many digits to write after the decimal separator, from 0 to 100. The default is 0, which writes no decimal separator.

params.name: decimalSeparator
params.descHtml: The text between the whole part and the decimals. The default is ..

params.name: groupSeparator
params.descHtml: The text between each group of three digits, counted from the right. The default is empty, so the digits are not grouped.

doc.returnHtml: The text. The number is rounded to decimals places, and a half is rounded away from zero. A negative number starts with -. A number that rounds to zero has no -.

errors.descHtml: When $n is INFINITY, -INFINITY or NaN, or when decimals is more than 100.
When $n is a uint larger than Core\Math::INT_MAX.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the hyperbolic sine of $n, which is (exp($n) - exp(-$n)) / 2.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: Any number.

doc.returnHtml: A number with the same sign as $n. It is INFINITY when $n is above about 710, and -INFINITY when $n is below about -710. NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of $n, which is (exp($n) + exp(-$n)) / 2.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: Any number.

doc.returnHtml: A number of at least 1.0. It is INFINITY when $n is above about 710 or below about -710. NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of $n. That is Core\Math::sinh divided by Core\Math::cosh.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: Any number.

doc.returnHtml: A number from -1.0 to 1.0, with the same sign as $n. INFINITY gives 1.0, -INFINITY gives -1.0 and NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine of $n. It undoes Core\Math::sinh.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: Any number.

doc.returnHtml: The number whose hyperbolic sine is $n. It has the same sign as $n. NaN gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the number whose hyperbolic cosine is $n. This is the inverse hyperbolic cosine.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: A hyperbolic cosine: a number that is 1.0 or more.

doc.returnHtml: A number that is 0.0 or more. A $n below 1.0 gives NaN.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the number whose hyperbolic tangent is $n. This is the inverse hyperbolic tangent. It undoes Core\Math::tanh.

params.name: n
params.descHtml: A hyperbolic tangent: a number from -1.0 to 1.0.

doc.returnHtml: A number with the same sign as $n. 1.0 gives INF and -1.0 gives -INF. A $n outside -1.0 to 1.0 gives NaN.

classes.summaryHtml: * is exponentiation and % is integer modulo, so neither has a member (R17). Division by zero throws ArithmeticError (R4) — in intDiv, in mod, and in the / operator whatever the operand types, which is exactly why fdiv is* a member here: it is the one spelling left for IEEE's INF, and PHP has it for the same reason. Overflow throws rather than becoming a float (rule:types/arithmetic).

doc.shortHtml: Runs $fn and returns everything it printed with echo. This replaces PHP's ob_start and ob_get_clean. The printed text does not reach the output. You can call capture inside another capture, and each call collects only what its own function printed.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: The function to run. Its return value is not used.

params.name: through
params.descHtml: A function that takes the collected Core\Cli\Text and returns a new Core\Cli\Text. capture returns that new text. Without it, capture returns the text as it was printed.

doc.returnHtml: What $fn printed, as a Core\Cli\Text. It is empty when $fn printed nothing. Use echo to print it, or its text method to get a string. Output from Core\Debug::dump is not collected.

errors.descHtml: The through function returned something that is not a Core\Cli\Text.

classes.name: Core\Path
classes.summary:
Pure string algebra over paths. **No member touches the disk**, so none needs a capability, and every member
but `fromCwd` is constant-foldable. Everything that reads or writes is `Core\IO` (§ 14) — that split is the
point. `fromCwd` reads the process's working directory, and throws while a request is being answered
(`rule:programs/path-literals-resolve-from-their-file`).

constants.name: SEPARATOR
constants.descHtml: The separator this platform's paths are rendered with — \ on Windows and / everywhere else, as DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR is; every member emits it and accepts both.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the last part of $path: the file name, or the name of the last folder. A separator at the end is ignored, so /srv/shop/ gives shop. This replaces PHP's basename.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

params.name: withoutExtension
params.descHtml: When true, the extension is removed, so report.pdf gives report. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The name. For a path that is only a root, such as / or C:\, the result is the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the folder that contains $path. The option levels goes up more than one folder. This replaces PHP's dirname.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

params.name: levels
params.descHtml: How many parts to remove from the end. The default is 1. With 0, the result is the path with its separators cleaned up. A number larger than the path stops at the root.

doc.returnHtml: The folder, written with Path::SEPARATOR. When nothing is left, the result is the root for an absolute path and . for a relative one. dirname('') is ., and PHP returns ''.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the extension of the last part of $path: the text after the last ., without the dot. This replaces PHP's pathinfo($path, PATHINFO_EXTENSION).

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: The extension, or null when there is none. A name that starts with a dot, such as .gitignore, has none. A name that ends with a dot, such as report., has none too. PHP returns gitignore and '' for these two.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $path with the extension of its last part changed to $extension. When $extension is null, the extension is removed. PHP has no function for this.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

params.name: extension
params.descHtml: The new extension, without its dot, the same way Core\Path::extension returns it. It may have a dot inside, such as tar.gz. null removes the extension.

doc.returnHtml: The new path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR.

errors.descHtml: $extension is empty, starts with a ., or contains / or \. Or $path has no file name, such as / or ''.

doc.shortHtml: Adds each of $segments to the end of $base, with one separator between each part. This replaces the $a . "/" . $b that PHP programs write. Only $base decides where the result starts. A segment that starts with / or a drive is added after $base and does not replace it.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The first path. The result starts where this path starts.

params.name: segments
params.descHtml: Any number of paths to add, in order. A leading /, \ or drive in one of them is removed.

doc.returnHtml: The joined path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. With no segments, the result is $base with its extra separators removed. A .. segment stays in the result and still means the parent folder.

doc.shortHtml: Splits $path into its parts: the folders and the file name, in order. This replaces PHP's explode("/", $path). Core\Path::join puts the parts back together into the same path.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: The parts in order. When the path starts at a root, the root is the first part: /, a drive such as C:\, or a share such as \\server\share\. The root is written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. No part is empty, because a repeated separator or one at the end adds nothing. The empty path gives an empty array.

members.name: normalize
members.replaces: the lexical half of `realpath` — resolves `.`/`..` **without** touching the disk

doc.shortHtml: Removes the . and .. parts from $path and writes it with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. The method works on the text only and never looks at the disk. The result can still point outside a folder, so it does not make a path safe. Core\IO::within checks that.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: The same path without . parts, and with each .. removing the folder before it. A .. at the start of a relative path stays. A .. that would go above a root is removed, because a root has no parent. A repeated separator or one at the end is removed. The empty path gives ..

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $path starts at a root. A root is a separator, a drive followed by a separator, or a network share. The check is the same on every platform.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. / and \ are both separators on every platform.

doc.returnHtml: true for /tmp, \tmp, C:/log and \\server\share. false for a relative path such as logs/app.log, for C:log, and for the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the path that leads from the folder $base to $path. The . and .. parts of both paths are removed first, as Core\Path::normalize does. PHP has no function for this.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The place the result leads to.

params.name: base
params.descHtml: The folder the result starts from. The result has one .. for each folder of $base that $path does not share.

doc.returnHtml: A relative path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR. It is . when both paths name the same place. It is null when no relative path exists: one path is absolute and the other is not, the paths start at different roots, or $base starts with more .. parts than $path does. Folder names are compared byte for byte. A drive letter and a server name ignore upper and lower case.

doc.shortHtml: Joins $path to the folder the program was started from, and returns the full path. Use it for a path that a user typed on the command line.

params.name: path
params.descHtml: The path. A relative path is joined to the working folder. A full path is returned as it is, with its . and .. parts removed.

doc.returnHtml: A full path, written with Core\Path::SEPARATOR, with its . and .. parts removed. The method does not check that the file exists. The result is not tainted, so you can pass a path from Core\Cli::arguments to Core\IO::read.

errors.descHtml: The program is answering a web request. A server has no working folder that belongs to the app.

classes.summaryHtml: Pure string algebra over paths. No member touches the disk, so none needs a capability, and every member but fromCwd is constant-foldable. Everything that reads or writes is Core\IO (§ 14) — that split is the point. fromCwd reads the process's working directory, and throws while a request is being answered (rule:programs/path-literals-resolve-from-their-file).

classes.name: Core\Random
classes.summary:
`Core\Random` is a CSPRNG, always — PHP's `rand`/`mt_rand`/`shuffle`/`str_shuffle`/`array_rand` and its
newer `Random\Randomizer` OOP twin all collapse into it, and none of the insecure generators survives
under any name.

doc.shortHtml: Draws an integer uniformly from [$min, $max], inclusive at both ends, from the CSPRNG — as random_int does, replacing rand and mt_rand as well.

params.name: min
params.descHtml: The lowest value the draw may answer.

params.name: max
params.descHtml: The highest value the draw may answer.

doc.returnHtml: An int in the range, without bias; $min itself when the two bounds are equal.

errors.descHtml: $min is above $max — the range is empty, and the bounds are not swapped.

doc.shortHtml: Draws a float uniformly from the half-open interval [0, 1), replacing lcg_value and the mt_rand() / mt_getrandmax() idiom.
doc.returnHtml: A float with 53 random bits; 0.0 is drawable and 1.0 is not.

doc.shortHtml: Draws $count bytes from the CSPRNG as a raw buffer — a key, a nonce or an IV — as random_bytes does, replacing openssl_random_pseudo_bytes as well.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: How many bytes to draw; at least one.

doc.returnHtml: A bytes value of exactly $count octets, unrendered — Core\Random::token is the hex spelling.

errors.descHtml: $count is 0, as random_bytes(0) is a ValueError, or is larger than a buffer this process can allocate.

doc.shortHtml: Draws $bytes bytes from the CSPRNG and renders them as lower-case hex — the bin2hex(random_bytes(…)) idiom, for a session identifier or a reset link.

params.name: bytes
params.descHtml: How many bytes of entropy to draw, 32 by default — the answer is twice as many characters.

doc.returnHtml: A string of 2 * $bytes hex digits, 0–9 and a–f.

errors.descHtml: $bytes is 0 — the empty string is a token every other empty token equals — or the draw or its rendering is larger than a buffer this process can allocate.

doc.shortHtml: Draws one entry of $a uniformly and answers its value, replacing array_rand in its one-element spelling — the value, where array_rand answers the key.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to draw from.

doc.returnHtml: One entry's value; null when $a is empty, which over an array<?T> is indistinguishable from drawing a null entry.

doc.shortHtml: Draws $count distinct entries of $a uniformly, replacing array_rand with a count — in random order, where array_rand keeps the subject's order.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to draw from.

params.name: count
params.descHtml: How many distinct entries to draw; at most the array's size.

doc.returnHtml: A fresh list of the drawn values under 0, 1, … keys, in random order; the subject's keys are discarded, and $a is unchanged.

errors.descHtml: $count is above the number of entries $a holds.

doc.shortHtml: Answers every entry of $a in a uniformly random order, replacing shuffle and str_shuffle — a fresh array rather than a reordering in place.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The array to reorder.

doc.returnHtml: A fresh list of all the values under 0, 1, … keys — the subject's keys are discarded, as shuffle renumbers — and $a is unchanged.

classes.summaryHtml: Core\Random is a CSPRNG, always — PHP's rand/mt_rand/shuffle/str_shuffle/array_rand and its newer Random\Randomizer OOP twin all collapse into it, and none of the insecure generators survives under any name.

classes.name: Core\Regex
classes.summary:
Semantics — the two-tier engine, the step budget, why the *pattern* is a sink while the subject is not —
are `rule:core-classes/regex-two-tiers`. `preg_match`'s `$matches` out-parameter is a returned
`?Match` (R3), and there are no `PREG_*` flag constants (R11).

doc.shortHtml: Compiles a regular expression once, with options, and returns a Core\Regex\Pattern. You can pass the Pattern to every Core\Regex method that takes a pattern.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: The regular expression, with no delimiters. A tainted string does not compile here. Use Core\Regex::quote to match a user's text literally.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: true makes letters match in upper and lower case. PHP writes this as i. The default is false.

params.name: multiline
params.descHtml: true makes ^ and $ match at the start and end of every line. PHP writes this as m. The default is false.

params.name: dotAll
params.descHtml: true makes . match a newline too. PHP writes this as s. The default is false.

params.name: ungreedy
params.descHtml: true makes and + match as little as possible, and ? as much as possible. PHP writes this as U. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The compiled Core\Regex\Pattern. The pattern is checked here, so a mistake in it throws at this line and not at its first use.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression. The message contains the pattern.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $pattern matches anywhere in $subject. The match can be at any position. Write ^ and $ in the pattern to match the whole text.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to search.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

doc.returnHtml: true if the text contains at least one match, and false if it does not.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, or matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows.

doc.shortHtml: Finds the first match of $pattern in $subject and returns it as a Core\Regex\Match. The Match has the matched text, each group and the position of the match.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to search.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

params.name: from
params.descHtml: The character position where the search starts. The default is 0. A negative position counts from the end of $subject.

doc.returnHtml: The first Core\Regex\Match at or after from, or null if there is no match.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, or matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows.

doc.shortHtml: Finds every match of $pattern in $subject and returns them as an array of Core\Regex\Match. The matches do not overlap, and they are in the order they appear in the text.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to search.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

doc.returnHtml: One Core\Regex\Match for each match, from left to right. The array is empty if there is no match.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, or matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces every match of $pattern in $subject with $replacement, and returns the new text. In $replacement, $1 is the text of group 1 and $0 is the whole match.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to search.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

params.name: replacement
params.descHtml: The text that replaces each match. $1 to $99 insert a numbered group, and ${name} inserts a named group. Write ${1}0 when a digit follows the group. $$ is one $. A group the pattern does not have inserts nothing. PHP's \1 is not a group here.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: How many matches to replace, counted from the start of the text. The default is every match. 0 replaces nothing.

doc.returnHtml: The text with the matches replaced. It is the same text if there is no match.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, or matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows.

members.signature: replaceWith(string $subject, Pattern|string $pattern, callable(Match): string $fn, {limit?: uint}): string

doc.shortHtml: Replaces every match of $pattern in $subject with the text your function returns for that match, and returns the new text. The function gets one Core\Regex\Match.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to search.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

params.name: fn
params.descHtml: A function that gets one Core\Regex\Match and returns a string. It is called once for each match, from left to right. The text it returns is inserted as it is, so $1 in it is two characters.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: How many matches to replace, counted from the start of the text. The default is every match. 0 replaces nothing. The function is not called for a match after the limit.

doc.returnHtml: The text with the matches replaced. It is the same text if there is no match.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows, or the new text is larger than the memory limit.

members.name: split
members.signature: split(string $subject, Pattern|string $pattern, {limit?: int, keepEmpty?: bool}): array<string>

doc.shortHtml: Splits $subject at every match of $pattern, and returns the pieces as an array. The matches are not part of any piece.

params.name: subject
params.descHtml: The text to split.

params.name: pattern
params.descHtml: A Core\Regex\Pattern from Core\Regex::compile, or a pattern string with no options. A tainted string does not compile here.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: The largest number of pieces. The last piece contains the rest of the text. A negative number removes that many pieces from the end. 0 returns the whole text as one piece. The default is no limit. PHP's preg_split reads 0 and -1 as no limit.

params.name: keepEmpty
params.descHtml: Whether empty pieces are kept. The default is true. With false, empty pieces are removed after limit is applied.

doc.returnHtml: The pieces, from left to right. If there is no match, the array has one piece: the whole text.

errors.descHtml: $pattern is not a valid regular expression, or matching it against $subject needs more steps than the limit allows.

doc.shortHtml: Puts a \ before every character that has a special meaning in a pattern. The result is a pattern that matches $literal exactly. A tainted text is allowed here, and the result can be used as a pattern.

params.name: literal
params.descHtml: The text to match exactly.

doc.returnHtml: The escaped pattern. A text with no special characters is returned unchanged. The escaped characters are not the same as PHP's preg_quote: & and ~ are escaped here, and !, :, <, =, > and / are not.

classes.summaryHtml: Semantics — the two-tier engine, the step budget, why the pattern is a sink while the subject is not — are rule:core-classes/regex-two-tiers. preg_match's $matches out-parameter is a returned ?Match (R3), and there are no PREG_* flag constants (R11).

doc.returnHtml: The text of the group. The result is null if the pattern has the group but this match did not use it.

errors.descHtml: The pattern has no group with this number or name.

members.notesHtml: every group at once, in preg_match's own order: a named group under its name, then under its number

doc.returnHtml: An array with group 0 first. A group that this match did not use is in the array, and its value is null.

doc.returnHtml: The position of the first character of the match. A match at the start of the text is at 0.
