doc.returnHtml: The matched text. It is never null, but it can be an empty string.

classes.name: Core\Str
classes.summary:
`string` is guaranteed-valid UTF-8 (`rule:types/bytes`), so **no member takes an
encoding argument** (R13) and there is no `mb_` twin of anything. Indexing granularity — what `length`, `at`
and `slice` count in — is `rule:types/string-is-utf8`'s, not this file's: **extended
grapheme clusters**. Every signature below is written granularity-agnostically, so nothing here changes if
that ADR's own *Revisiting* ever re-opens it.

doc.shortHtml: Which of UAX #15's four normal forms Core\Str::normalize rewrites into — composed or decomposed on one axis, canonical or compatibility on the other.

cases.name: Nfc
cases.descHtml: Canonical composition: é is one code point, and only canonical equivalents are unified — the form to store and compare text in.

cases.name: Nfd
cases.descHtml: Canonical decomposition: é is e plus a combining acute, and only canonical equivalents are unified.

cases.name: Nfkc
cases.descHtml: Compatibility composition: Nfc, and a character that merely renders like another — ﬁ, ① — is unified with it too, which does not round-trip.

cases.name: Nfkd
cases.descHtml: Compatibility decomposition: Nfd, plus the same compatibility unification Nfkc applies.

doc.shortHtml: Counts the graphemes in $s — user-perceived characters, the unit every Core\Str member counts in — so a combining sequence counts once and this is never a byte count.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to measure.

doc.returnHtml: The grapheme count; 0 for the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s is the empty string "". A string of spaces is not empty, and neither is "0".

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to check.

doc.returnHtml: true when $s has no characters, otherwise false.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the one character at position $index of $s. A character is what a person sees as one letter, so "é" is one character. Replaces PHP's mb_substr($s, $i, 1).

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to read from.

params.name: index
params.descHtml: The position of the character. The first character is at 0. A negative position counts from the end, so -1 is the last character.

doc.returnHtml: A string with exactly one character in it.

errors.descHtml: There is no character at $index. The position is at or past the length of $s, counting from either end.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $needle appears anywhere in $haystack. Replaces PHP's str_contains.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The text to search for. The search is case-sensitive.

doc.returnHtml: true when $needle is in $haystack, otherwise false. An empty $needle is in every string, so the result is true.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s starts with $prefix. Replaces PHP's str_starts_with.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to check.

params.name: prefix
params.descHtml: The text $s must start with. The check is case-sensitive.

doc.returnHtml: true when $s starts with $prefix, otherwise false. An empty $prefix is at the start of every string, so the result is true.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s ends with $suffix. Replaces PHP's str_ends_with.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to check.

params.name: suffix
params.descHtml: The text $s must end with. The check is case-sensitive.

doc.returnHtml: true when $s ends with $suffix, otherwise false. An empty $suffix is at the end of every string, so the result is true.

doc.shortHtml: Finds the first place where $needle appears in $haystack and returns its position. The first character is position 0. Replaces PHP's strpos, stripos, mb_strpos and mb_stripos.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The string to search for. An empty needle matches where the search starts.

params.name: from
params.descHtml: The position where the search starts. A negative value counts from the end. The default is 0.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: When true, upper-case and lower-case letters match each other. Each character is compared by its lower-case form, so ß does not match SS. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The position of the first match at or after from, counted in characters as Core\Str::length counts them. You can pass it to Core\Str::slice. The result is null when there is no match.

doc.shortHtml: Finds the last place where $needle appears in $haystack and returns its position. The first character is position 0. Replaces PHP's strrpos, strripos and mb_strrpos.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The string to search for.

params.name: before
params.descHtml: Searches only the characters in front of this position, so a match must end here or earlier. A negative position counts back from the end. The default is the whole string.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: When true, upper-case and lower-case letters count as the same. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The position of the last match, or null when there is none. Matches may overlap, so lastIndexOf("aaa", "aa") returns 1.

doc.shortHtml: Counts how many times $needle appears in $haystack. Replaces PHP's substr_count.

params.name: haystack
params.descHtml: The string to search in.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The text to count. The search is case-sensitive. It must not be empty.

doc.returnHtml: The number of times $needle appears, or 0 when it does not appear. Matches do not overlap, so countOf("aaa", "aa") is 1.

errors.descHtml: $needle is empty.

members.name: compare
members.signature: compare(string $a, string $b, {caseInsensitive?: bool, natural?: bool}): int

doc.shortHtml: Compares two strings to sort them. Replaces PHP's strcmp, strcasecmp, strnatcmp and strnatcasecmp.

params.name: a
params.descHtml: The first string.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The second string.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: When true, upper and lower case letters are equal. ß and SS are still different. The default is false.

params.name: natural
params.descHtml: When true, digits inside the strings are compared as numbers, so "img2" comes before "img12". The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: -1 when $a comes first, 0 when the two are equal, and 1 when $b comes first.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the part of $s that starts at $offset and has $length characters. Positions count characters as a person sees them, so "é" is one character. Replaces PHP's substr and mb_substr.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to take the part from.

params.name: offset
params.descHtml: Where the part starts. The first character is at 0. A negative offset counts from the end.

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many characters to take. A negative length stops that many characters before the end. null takes everything to the end.

doc.returnHtml: The part as a new string. It is "" when the part is empty or the offset is past the end. $s does not change.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the part of $s before the first $needle, without the needle. With {last: true}, it cuts at the last $needle. Replaces PHP's strstr($s, $needle, true).

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to cut.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The separator to cut at. The search is case-sensitive. The needle is not part of the result.

params.name: last
params.descHtml: When true, cuts at the last needle. The default is false, which cuts at the first one.

doc.returnHtml: The text before the needle. If the needle is not in $s, the result is null. If the needle is at the start, the result is an empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the part of $s after the first $needle, without the needle. With {last: true}, it cuts at the last $needle. Replaces PHP's strstr and strrchr.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to cut.

params.name: needle
params.descHtml: The separator to cut at. The search is case-sensitive. The needle is not part of the result.

params.name: last
params.descHtml: When true, cuts at the last needle. The default is false, which cuts at the first one.

doc.returnHtml: The text after the needle. If the needle is not in $s, the result is null. If the needle is at the end, the result is an empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Splits $s into parts at every place where $separator is found. Replaces PHP's explode.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to split.

params.name: separator
params.descHtml: The text to split at. Upper and lower case are different. It must not be empty.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: A positive limit gives at most that many parts. The last part contains the rest of the string. A negative limit deletes that many parts from the end. 0 gives the whole string as one part. The default is no limit.

doc.returnHtml: The parts in order, without the separator. The empty string gives [""]. A negative limit that deletes every part gives [].

errors.descHtml: $separator is empty.

doc.shortHtml: Divides $s into pieces of $size characters each. A piece never cuts a character in half. Replaces PHP's str_split, mb_str_split and chunk_split.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to divide.

params.name: size
params.descHtml: How many characters each piece has. It must be at least 1.

doc.returnHtml: The pieces in order. Only the last piece can be shorter than $size. The result is [] for the empty string.

errors.descHtml: $size is 0.

doc.shortHtml: Splits $s into its lines. A line ends at \n, at \r\n or at \r, on every system. Replaces PHP's explode(PHP_EOL, $s).

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to split.

doc.returnHtml: One string for each line, without its line break. A line break at the very end does not add an empty line. An empty line in the middle is kept as "". An empty string gives [].

doc.shortHtml: Divides $s into its characters, the way a person counts them. An accented letter, a flag or an emoji with a skin tone is one character, even when it is several code points. These are the characters Core\Str::length counts. Replaces PHP's grapheme_str_split.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to divide.

doc.returnHtml: One string for each character, in order. An empty string gives [].

doc.shortHtml: Lists the code points of $s. A code point is the number Unicode gives to one symbol. One character a person sees can be several code points. Replaces PHP's mb_str_split followed by mb_ord.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to read.

doc.returnHtml: One uint for each code point, in order. Each number is between 0 and 0x10FFFF and is never a surrogate. The result is [] for the empty string.

doc.shortHtml: Joins the strings in $parts into one string, with $separator between each two neighbouring strings. Replaces PHP's implode.

params.name: parts
params.descHtml: The strings to join, in the order of the array.

params.name: separator
params.descHtml: The text that goes between two neighbouring strings. The default is the empty string "".

doc.returnHtml: The joined string. An empty array gives "".

doc.shortHtml: Replaces every occurrence of $search in $s with $replacement. Matches are found from left to right and do not overlap. The new text is not searched again. Replaces PHP's str_replace and str_ireplace.

params.descHtml: The string to change.

params.name: search

params.name: replacement
params.descHtml: The text that replaces each match.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: If true, upper-case and lower-case letters match each other, so "A" finds "a". The default is false.

params.name: limit
params.descHtml: The most matches to replace, counted from the left. 0 replaces nothing. The default is every match.

doc.returnHtml: The changed string. If nothing matched, the result is $s unchanged.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces several texts in $s in one call. Each key of $pairs is a text to find, and its value is the text that replaces it. The string is read once, from left to right. Where several keys match at the same place, the longest one is used. The new text is not searched again. Replaces PHP's strtr and str_replace with arrays.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

params.name: pairs
params.descHtml: The replacements. Each key is the text to find, and its value is the text that replaces it. An empty key is ignored.

params.name: caseInsensitive
params.descHtml: If true, upper-case and lower-case letters match each other. If two keys then match the same text, the key written first is used. The default is false.

doc.returnHtml: The changed string. If $pairs is empty or nothing matched, the result is $s unchanged.

doc.shortHtml: Replaces a part of $s with $replacement. The part is the text Core\Str::slice returns for the same $offset and $length. Replaces PHP's substr_replace.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to change.

params.name: offset

params.name: length
params.descHtml: How many characters the part has. A negative length stops that many characters before the end. null means the part runs to the end.

params.name: replacement
params.descHtml: The text that replaces the part. "" deletes the part.

doc.shortHtml: Removes the given characters from both ends of $s. Replaces PHP's trim.

params.descHtml: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.descHtml: The characters to remove, in any order. a..z is the three characters a, . and z. The default is space, tab, newline, carriage return, NUL and vertical tab.

doc.returnHtml: $s without those characters at its start and its end. The middle of $s is not changed.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.descHtml: The characters to remove, in any order. a..z is the three characters a, . and z. The default is space, tab, newline, carriage return, NUL and vertical tab.

doc.returnHtml: $s without those characters at its start. The rest of $s is not changed.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to trim.

params.name: characters
params.descHtml: The characters to remove, in any order. a..z is the three characters a, . and z. The default is space, tab, newline, carriage return, NUL and vertical tab.

doc.returnHtml: $s without those characters at its end. The rest of $s is not changed.

params.name: length

params.name: padding
params.descHtml: The text to add. The last copy is cut short when only part of it fits. The default is one space.

doc.returnHtml: The padded string. If $s already has $length characters or more, it is returned unchanged.

errors.descHtml: $padding is empty and $s is shorter than $length. It is also thrown when the result is larger than this process can hold.

doc.shortHtml: Returns $times copies of $s, joined into one string. Replaces PHP's str_repeat.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The string to repeat.

params.name: times
params.descHtml: How many copies to write.

When deadline runs out before every task has finished. Every task is stopped first, and the call waits until they have stopped.

classes.name: Core\Time
classes.summary:
PHP has ~40 `date_*` procedural functions that are aliases of `DateTime` methods, *and* a
`DateTime`/`DateTimeImmutable` mutable/immutable pair. Both duplications are gone (R17, R20): there are
objects only, and every one is immutable. There is **no ambient timezone** — no process default, no
per-request default — so a `Zone` is an explicit argument at every instant↔calendar conversion.

**Two arithmetics, and the type says which one you get.** An `Instant` moves by a `Duration`, which is an
exact count of nanoseconds; a `DateTime` moves by a count of a `Unit`, which is a calendar step that a DST
boundary or a short month can make longer or shorter than its nominal length. `Time::now()->plus(72h)` and
`Time::now()->in($zone)->plus(3, Unit::Day)` are different operations, and PHP's `"+3 days"` is ambiguous
between them. There is no relative-expression string anywhere in this class: everything `strtotime` spells
is a typed call, and `rule:types/duration-literal`'s `72h`/`30d` literal is what keeps them
short.

doc.shortHtml: A day of the week, Monday first as ISO 8601 and date("N") order them — what $d->weekday() answers and next/previous take. The order is theirs and the numbering is not: the cases are zero-based, Monday as int is 0 and Sunday is 6, where date("N") numbers that same order 1 through 7.

The moment the link stops working. It is inside the signature, so nobody can change it. null means the link never expires. A link that never expires works for anybody who finds it later, for example in a browser history.

errors.descHtml: $keys is empty, or one of its keys is not 32 bytes long.

The link was not signed with these keys. This is the case when a parameter was added, removed or changed, when the token was changed, when the key was removed from the list, when there is no _sig, and when there are two. All of these give the same message. An expired link gives a different message.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the scheme of the address, which is the part before the first :. For https://example.com/ the result is https. The scheme is returned as it was written, so HTTPS stays upper case.
doc.returnHtml: The scheme, without the :. The result is null when the address has no scheme, such as /about or //example.com/.

members.name: userInfo
members.notes: one reader, not `user`/`pass` — RFC 3986 § 3.2.1 deprecates the split form
members.notesHtml: one reader, not user/pass — RFC 3986 § 3.2.1 deprecates the split form

doc.shortHtml: Returns the user part of the address, which is the text between // and @. For ftp://ann@files.example.com/ the result is ann. A password written as ann:secret is returned as one text. Escapes such as %40 stay in it.
doc.returnHtml: The user part, without the @. The result is null when the address has no @ before its host. It is "" when nothing is written before the @.

members.name: host
members.notes: `null` where no authority was written, `""` where an empty one was
members.notesHtml: null where no authority was written, "" where an empty one was

doc.shortHtml: Returns the host of the address, such as example.com. The host is returned as it was written, so upper-case letters stay upper case. An IPv6 address keeps its brackets, such as [::1].
doc.returnHtml: The host. The result is null when the address has no // part. It is "" when the // part is empty, as in file:///tmp.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the port of the address as a number. For http://example.com:8080/ the result is 8080.
doc.returnHtml: The port, from 0 to 65535. The result is null when the address has no port. It is also null when the : has no digits after it, as in http://example.com:/. A default port, such as 443 for https, is never filled in.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the path of the address. For https://example.com/docs/guide?page=2 the result is /docs/guide. The path is returned as it was written, so escapes such as %20 and parts such as /../ stay in it.
doc.returnHtml: The path. It is never null. An address with no path, such as https://example.com, returns "".

doc.shortHtml: Returns the query of the address, which is the text after the ?. For https://example.com/search?q=shoes#top the result is q=shoes. Escapes such as %20 stay in it, and Core\Uri::parseQuery reads it into an array.
doc.returnHtml: The query, without the ?. The result is null when the address has no ?. It is "" when nothing is written after the ?.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the fragment of the address, which is the text after the #. For https://example.com/guide#install the result is install. Escapes such as %20 stay in it, and Core\Uri::decodeComponent decodes them.
doc.returnHtml: The fragment, without the #. The result is null when the address has no #. It is "" when nothing is written after the #.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the address as text. For a Uri from Core\Uri::parse, this is exactly the text that was read. Upper-case letters and escapes such as %2f do not change. echo $uri prints the same text.
doc.returnHtml: The address as a string. For HTTP://Example.COM/a%2fb the result is HTTP://Example.COM/a%2fb.

doc.shortHtml: Creates a new random UUID, such as f9168c5e-ceb2-4faa-b6bf-329bf39fa1e4. 122 of its 128 bits come from a secure random number generator. The other six bits say that it is a version 4 UUID.
doc.returnHtml: A new Uuid. Nobody can guess it, and it contains no date or time, so it is safe to show to other people.

doc.shortHtml: Creates a new UUID that starts with the current time, such as 0190d1e6-8e3c-7c2a-9a4b-1f2e3d4c5b6a. The first 48 bits are the number of milliseconds since 1970. 74 of the other bits are random. Use it as a database key, because new keys sort after older ones.
doc.returnHtml: A new Uuid. It sorts after every UUID created in an earlier millisecond. Two UUIDs created in the same millisecond sort in a random order. Anybody who has the UUID can read the time it was created, so use Core\Uuid::v4 for an ID that other people see. If the computer's clock is before 1970, the time part is zero.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the text $s as a UUID. The text must be 32 hexadecimal digits in groups of 8, 4, 4, 4 and 12, joined by hyphens, such as f9168c5e-ceb2-4faa-b6bf-329bf39fa1e4. Upper case and lower case letters are both allowed.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to read. It must be exactly 36 characters long.

doc.returnHtml: The Uuid that the text gives. The version digit is not checked, so the nil UUID (all zeros) and the max UUID (all f) are both valid.

errors.descHtml: $s is not in that form. The 32 digits without hyphens, a UUID in {} braces and a UUID after urn:uuid: all throw this error too. The message quotes up to 48 characters of $s.

doc.shortHtml: Reads the text $s as a UUID, like Core\Uuid::parse. When the text is not a UUID, it returns null and does not throw an error. Use it to check whether a text is a UUID.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to read. It must be 32 hexadecimal digits in groups of 8, 4, 4, 4 and 12, joined by hyphens. Upper case and lower case letters are both allowed.

doc.returnHtml: The Uuid that the text gives, or null when the text is in any other form. The 32 digits without hyphens, a UUID in {} braces and a UUID after urn:uuid: all give null.

doc.shortHtml: Reads sixteen bytes as a UUID. Many databases store a UUID in a binary column in this form, and binary protocols send it this way.

params.name: b
params.descHtml: The sixteen bytes, in the same order as the digits of the UUID's text. $uuid->toBytes() gives them in this order.

doc.returnHtml: The Uuid that the bytes give. Any sixteen bytes are a valid UUID, so only the length is checked.

errors.descHtml: $b is not exactly sixteen bytes long. The message gives the length of $b.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the text of the UUID, such as f9168c5e-ceb2-4faa-b6bf-329bf39fa1e4. The digits are in groups of 8, 4, 4, 4 and 12, joined by hyphens. echo $uuid writes the same text.
doc.returnHtml: A string of 36 characters. The letters are always lower case, even when parse read them in upper case.

doc.shortHtml: Returns the sixteen bytes of the UUID. Use it to store a UUID in a binary database column or to send it in a binary message. The text form of the same UUID is 36 bytes long.
doc.returnHtml: Sixteen bytes, in the same order as the digits of the UUID's text. Core\Uuid::fromBytes reads them back as the same UUID.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s is an email address, such as ada@example.com. The part before the @ has at most 64 characters: letters, digits, single dots and some symbols such as + and _. The part after the @ is a domain name with at least one dot. The whole address has at most 254 characters.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to test.

doc.returnHtml: true for an email address. false for anything else, for example a space, two dots in a row, quotes, an address such as a@[192.0.2.1], a domain without a dot such as a@localhost, or a character that is not ASCII. The method does not check whether the address exists.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s is an IP address. An IPv4 address is four numbers from 0 to 255 joined by dots, such as 192.0.2.1. An IPv6 address is up to eight groups of hex digits joined by :, such as 2001:db8::1.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to test.

params.name: version
params.descHtml: 4 accepts only IPv4 addresses, and 6 accepts only IPv6 addresses. Without it, both are accepted.

doc.returnHtml: true for an IP address of the chosen version. false for anything else. A number with a leading zero, such as 192.0.2.01, gives false. An IPv6 address with a zone at the end, such as fe80::1%eth0, also gives false.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s is a MAC address, the hardware address of a network card. It is six pairs of hex digits joined by : or by -, such as 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e. It can also be three groups of four hex digits joined by ., such as 001a.2b3c.4d5e.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to test.

doc.returnHtml: true for one of the three ways to write it, in upper or lower case. false otherwise. A text that mixes two separators, such as 00:1a-2b:3c:4d:5e, gives false.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s is a domain name, such as example.com. A domain name has one or more parts joined by single dots. Each part has 1 to 63 letters, digits or -, and does not start or end with -. The whole name has at most 253 characters.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to test.

doc.returnHtml: true for a domain name. localhost and a name of digits such as 1.2.3.4 are true too. false for an empty part, a dot at the end, a part that starts or ends with -, or a character that is not ASCII. The method does not check whether the name exists.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether every character of $s is an ASCII character. ASCII has 128 characters: the English letters, the digits, common punctuation and the control characters. Each of them is one byte, from 0x00 to 0x7F.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to test.

doc.returnHtml: true when every character is ASCII, and true for the empty string. false when the text contains any other character, such as é or 日.

doc.shortHtml: Checks whether $s contains no control characters. A control character has no visible form, for example a tab, a new line or the null byte. Letters from any language, such as é or 日, are printable.

params.name: s
params.descHtml: The text to test.

doc.returnHtml: true when the text has no control character, and true for the empty string. false for a tab, a new line, a carriage return, DEL or any other control character. Some invisible characters are not control characters, such as the zero-width joiner. They give true, so this method does not find text that hides what it really says.
